name: managed-docker-crash-recovery
goal: Prove that a restarted offline Docker task supervisor reclaims a killed supervisor’s task container with daemon, owner and workspace evidence while concurrent live tasks and shared Docker resources survive.

evidence: Parent run-112 on MB2 proved SIGKILL leaves one running fixture and owner-plus-bind-scoped cleanup preserves the live bystander. On a later managed launch, reclaim the verified orphan automatically.

Extend the existing module-tasks Linux process lifecycle case beyond exit 37 and cancellation to a SIGKILL with an independent live managed supervisor and another launch. Reuse local pinned image and isolated workspaces.

MB2 Docker Desktop 29.4.0, one worker and cached no-network image. Commit 46f050ac45 reported recovered:false after the next managed launch. Exit 37, cancellation, live bystander and cached-image assertions passed. Sealed Harness regression 833611546695051f2131398bfd3b4cc0992a635eb920741cd7890e5ed461a2fe.
